questions.question: A state-dependent capacity rule fixes the capacity $c_k$ of week $k$ as a function of the queue, where $L_k$ is the queue length at the end of week $k$, $a_k$ the arrivals and $d_k$ the departures in week $k$. Which quantity may the rule use when $c_k$ is planned?
options: The queue length $L_k$ at the end of week $k$ itself
The arrivals $a_k$ that will come in during week $k$
The queue length $L_{k-1}$ at the end of the previous week
The departures $d_k$ that will be realised in week $k$

questions.question: A waiting list evolves by $d_k=\min\{L_{k-1}+a_k,c_k\}$ and $L_k=L_{k-1}+a_k-d_k$, with arrivals $a_k$, capacity $c_k$, departures $d_k$ and end-of-week queue $L_k$. A constant capacity is replaced by a rule $c_k=g(L_{k-1})$; the arrivals do not react to the rule. Which sequences can change as a result?
options: $\{c_k\}$, $\{d_k\}$ and $\{L_k\}$ can all change
Only $\{c_k\}$; departures and queue lengths stay as before
$\{c_k\}$ and $\{d_k\}$, while the queue lengths $\{L_k\}$ stay the same
$\{c_k\}$ and $\{L_k\}$, while the departures $\{d_k\}$ stay the same

questions.question: Arrivals per week have mean $\lambda$, and a state-dependent rule gives capacity $g(L)<\lambda$ whenever the previous queue length $L$ lies in the low region $L\le\alpha$ of the rule. For a queue in that region long enough to use its full capacity, what are the sign of the drift and its meaning?
options: Negative drift: the queue tends to shrink within this region
Positive drift: the queue tends to grow out of this region
Positive drift: the queue tends to shrink, as capacity is fully used
Zero drift: the rule adapts capacity, so the queue stays put

questions.question: Weekly capacity follows $c_k=12+e$ if $L_{k-1}\ge48$, $c_k=12$ if $24<L_{k-1}<48$ and $c_k=12-e$ if $L_{k-1}\le24$, with $L_k$ the queue length at the end of week $k$ and $e>0$. What does $H_n=\sum_{k=1}^n\mathbf{1}\{L_{k-1}\ge48\}$ count?
options: The number of weeks $1,\dots,n$ ending with at least $48$ in queue
The total extra capacity added over the weeks $1,\dots,n$
The number of patients waiting beyond the first $48$ places
The number of weeks $1,\dots,n$ in which the capacity was $12+e$

questions.question: Weekly capacity follows $c_k=12+e$ if $L_{k-1}\ge48$, $c_k=12$ if $24<L_{k-1}<48$ and $c_k=12-e$ if $L_{k-1}\le24$, with $L_k$ the queue length at the end of week $k$ and control size $e>0$. What can be said about the average capacity $\frac{1}{n}\sum_{k=1}^n c_k$ over weeks $1,\dots,n$?
options: It is always $12$, because the steps $+e$ and $-e$ around $12$ are symmetric
It is always above $12$, because the control can only add capacity
It is $12$ only if weeks with $L_{k-1}\ge48$ and with $L_{k-1}\le24$ are equally many
It is $12$ only if the queue is between $24$ and $48$ in at least half of the weeks

questions.question: Weekly capacity follows $c_k=12+e$ if $L_{k-1}\ge48$, $c_k=12$ if $24<L_{k-1}<48$ and $c_k=12-e$ if $L_{k-1}\le24$, with $L_k$ the queue length at the end of week $k$ and $e=3$. Which capacities $c_k$ belong to $L_{k-1}=24$, $L_{k-1}=36$ and $L_{k-1}=48$, in this order?

Weekly capacity follows $c_k=12+e$ if $L_{k-1}\ge48$, $c_k=12$ if $24<L_{k-1}<48$ and $c_k=12-e$ if $L_{k-1}\le24$ with $e=2$; jobs can be served in the week they arrive, $d_k=\min\{L_{k-1}+a_k,c_k\}$ and $L_k=L_{k-1}+a_k-d_k$. If $L_{k-1}=20$ and $a_k=7$, what is $L_k$?

A queue uses the capacity rule $c_k=3\cdot\mathbf{1}\{L_{k-1}>6\}$, where $L_k$ is the queue length at the end of week $k$, and evolves by $d_k=\min\{L_{k-1}+a_k,c_k\}$ and $L_k=L_{k-1}+a_k-d_k$ with arrivals $a_k$. If $L_{k-1}=5$ and $a_k=4$, what is $L_k$?

Arrivals per week have mean $\lambda=11.8$ and capacity follows $c_k=12+e$ if $L_{k-1}\ge48$, $c_k=12$ if $24<L_{k-1}<48$ and $c_k=12-e$ if $L_{k-1}\le24$ with $e=3$. What is the drift $\mathbb{E}[L_k-L_{k-1}\mid L_{k-1}=60]$ of the queue, which then uses its full capacity?

A waiting list evolves by $d_k=\min\{L_{k-1}+a_k,c_k\}$ and $L_k=L_{k-1}+a_k-d_k$ under some state-dependent capacity rule. Over $50$ weeks, $590$ patients arrive, the list has $L_0=30$ patients at the start and $L_{50}=42$ at the end. How many intakes $\sum_{k=1}^{50}d_k$ were done?

A queue evolves by $d_k=\min\{L_{k-1}+a_k,c_k\}$ and $L_k=L_{k-1}+a_k-d_k$ with arrivals $a_k$ unaffected by the capacity. For which capacity rules does $\sum_{k=1}^nd_k=\sum_{k=1}^na_k-(L_n-L_0)$ hold over every horizon $n$?
options: Only for rules whose average capacity equals the mean arrival rate
Only for rules with as many high-capacity weeks as low-capacity weeks
Only for constant capacity, since $c_k=g(L_{k-1})$ makes $d_k$ path-dependent
For every capacity rule, as it comes from summing $L_k-L_{k-1}=a_k-d_k$

questions.question: Arrivals per week have mean $\lambda=11.8$ and capacity follows $c_k=12+e$ if $L_{k-1}\ge48$, $c_k=12$ if $24<L_{k-1}<48$ and $c_k=12-e$ if $L_{k-1}\le24$. In simulations the queue stays controlled for $e=1$, $2$ and $5$ but fluctuates most for $e=1$. Which explanation fits the drift in the regions of the rule?
options: For larger $e$ the drift outside the band is larger in size, so the queue is pushed back faster
For larger $e$ the drift inside the band is larger in size, so the queue moves less there
Larger $e$ raises the average capacity well above $12$, so the queue stays short
Larger $e$ lets more patients be taken in overall, which removes the fluctuations

questions.question: An $(s,S)$ inventory policy orders up to level $S$ at the start of a period whenever the inventory position at the end of the previous period is $s$ or below. A clinic sets weekly capacity by $c_k=12+e$ if $L_{k-1}\ge48$, $c_k=12$ if $24<L_{k-1}<48$ and $c_k=12-e$ if $L_{k-1}\le24$, where $L_k$ is the queue at the end of week $k$. Which feature do the two rules share?
options: The controlled state is kept exactly at a single target value
The control also changes the demand or arrivals it reacts to
An action is triggered when an observed state crosses a fixed threshold
The decision for a period uses the demand or arrivals of that same period

questions.question: A clinic starts with $L_0=46$ waiting patients and sets capacity $c_k=15$ if $L_{k-1}\ge48$, $c_k=12$ if $24<L_{k-1}<48$ and $c_k=9$ if $L_{k-1}\le24$, with $L_k$ the list at the end of week $k$. Patients may be taken in during their arrival week. For arrivals $(a_1,a_2,a_3)=(15,8,10)$, what is $L_3$?

Weekly capacity follows $c_k=12+e$ if $L_{k-1}\ge48$, $c_k=12$ if $24<L_{k-1}<48$ and $c_k=12-e$ if $L_{k-1}\le24$ with $e=2$, where $L_k$ is the queue length at the end of week $k$. The queue lengths are $(L_0,L_1,\dots,L_5)=(30,48,22,20,36,52)$. What is the average capacity $\frac{1}{5}\sum_{k=1}^5c_k$ over weeks $1$ to $5$?

Arrivals per week have mean $\lambda=9.5$. A capacity rule gives $c_k$ the values $x$, $y$, $z$ for $L_{k-1}\le10$, $10<L_{k-1}<30$ and $L_{k-1}\ge30$. Which triple $(x,y,z)$ makes a queue using full capacity drift upward when $L_{k-1}\le10$ and downward when $L_{k-1}\ge30$?

A queue evolves by $d_k=\min\{L_{k-1}+a_k,c_k\}$ and $L_k=L_{k-1}+a_k-d_k$ with arrivals $a_k\ge0$ and capacity $c_k=c\,\mathbf{1}\{L_{k-1}>\alpha\}$, where $0<c<\alpha$ and $L_0>0$. Which argument shows $L_k>0$ for all $k$?
options: Every week brings at least one arrival, $a_k\ge1$, so $L_k\ge L_{k-1}$ and the queue cannot drop to zero
With $c<\alpha$ the drift $\lambda-c$ is positive, so the queue grows on average and stays positive
Capacity $c<\alpha$ stays below the arrival rate $\alpha$, so service never catches up with the arrivals
In a week with $L_{k-1}>\alpha>c$, $L_k\ge L_{k-1}-c>0$; otherwise $c_k=0$ and $L_k\ge L_{k-1}$

questions.question: Weekly arrivals are i.i.d. with mean $\lambda=11.8$ and take every value in $\{0,1,\dots,30\}$ with positive probability. Capacity follows $c_k=12+e$ if $L_{k-1}\ge48$, $c_k=12$ if $24<L_{k-1}<48$ and $c_k=12-e$ if $L_{k-1}\le24$ with $e=1$, and jobs can be served in their arrival week. Once $24<L_{k-1}<48$, is the queue sure to stay in this band?
options: Yes: the drift in the band is $-0.2$, so the queue only drifts slowly down to $24$
No: the drift gives only the expected change, and one busy week can lift it above $48$
Yes, provided $e$ is large enough that the drift outside the band is strong
No, because the rule lowers the arrivals whenever the queue has become long

questions.question: Capacity follows $c_k=12+e$ if $L_{k-1}\ge48$, $c_k=12$ if $24<L_{k-1}<48$ and $c_k=12-e$ if $L_{k-1}\le24$ with $e=2$. Over $n=100$ weeks the full capacity is used every week ($d_k=c_k$), $\sum_{k=1}^{100}a_k=1180$ and $L_{100}=L_0$. With $H_n$ and $D_n$ the numbers of weeks with $L_{k-1}\ge48$ and with $L_{k-1}\le24$, what is $D_n-H_n$?

Arrivals per week have mean $\lambda=12.5$ and capacity follows $c_k=12+e$ if $L_{k-1}\ge48$, $c_k=12$ if $24<L_{k-1}<48$ and $c_k=12-e$ if $L_{k-1}\le24$ with $e=2$. For queues using full capacity, at which queue length does the drift change from upward to downward?
options: At $48$: the drift is $+0.5$ in the band and $-1.5$ from $48$ on
At $24$: the drift is positive below $24$ and negative in the band
At $36$, the middle of the band, because the steps are symmetric
Nowhere: drift is positive in two regions, so the queue grows
